chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'ah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'For a man who has children, is it permissible for him to bequeath his wealth to his relatives?' He said: 'It is his wealth; he does with it what he wills until death comes to him.'

key_terms.يَصْنَعُ بِهِ مَا شَاءَ: he does with it what he wills

ai.seo_question: Can a father with children leave his entire estate to his relatives instead of his children?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of unrestricted testamentary freedom (*al-wasiyya*), affirming that a father retains full ownership and discretion over his wealth until death. This ruling underscores the distinction between the fixed shares of inheritance (*fara'id*) and the voluntary bequest, allowing the testator to allocate assets to relatives beyond their statutory portions, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding estate planning.
